history.summary: Removed the query-string and form-body api_key API authentication transports for 0.13.0, per the prior release's announced removal. Re-validated every section-0 fact against the current repository before writing code and found zero discrepancies. In middleware/middleware.go's extractExplicitAPICredential: query/form api_key presence is still detected via a new unsupportedTransport bool field (so a request carrying one can never silently fall back to session authentication and so CSRFExceptions' presence-based exemption continues to apply unchanged), but their values are no longer folded into the Bearer/raw 'values' slice used for lookup/ambiguity computation -- only r.Header.Values("Authorization") feeds that slice now. RequireAPIKey's single existing rejection branch (malformed || ambiguous || value=="" || unsupportedTransport) now also covers unsupportedTransport, sharing the exact same single limiter.RecordFailure(clientIP) call and the exact same 401 'Invalid API Key' JSON response as every other invalid-credential reason -- no new error message, no second rejection path, no new rate-limiter category. Raw/Bearer Authorization and session authentication are completely unchanged. Inverted every previously-passing query/form-success subtest to assert 401 rejection in middleware/api_auth_test.go, middleware/api_auth_form_fields_test.go, and controllers/api/campaign_transport_deprecation_test.go (the latter's trailing-slash route-matching regression guard was switched from the now-always-rejected query transport to a valid Authorization: Bearer header, so a non-200 result there can only mean a route mismatch, never ambiguity with the new removed-transport rejection). Added the full section-8 test matrix: non-empty/empty/no-equals query and form values, query/form plus a valid session (asserted via IsSessionAuthentication, not just status), query/form plus a simultaneously-valid Authorization header (including an identical-value case proving the coincidence does not rescue it), combined query+form in one request proven to record exactly one rate-limiter failure (not two), the same single-failure proof for query/Authorization and form/Authorization combinations, a blocked-IP pre-check proof that a removed-transport request gets 429 directly without needing a valid-looking token, and a dedicated CSRF regression test proving a query/form-only (no Authorization header at all) request retains the unsafe-method CSRF exemption. Updated all four canonical docs (API_AUTHENTICATION.md, API_KEY_TRANSPORT_DEPRECATION.md, RELEASE_NOTE_API_KEY_TRANSPORT_DEPRECATION.md, GROUP_IMPORT_LIMITS.md) to describe query/form as removed-in-0.13.0 (past/completed state), keep raw Authorization's deprecated/no-removal-version status and Bearer's canonical status unchanged, keep the historical 'Before' migration examples labeled as such, and explicitly state the removal prevents only future acceptance and cannot retroactively redact anything already logged. Replaced docsguard's two narrow literal-bounded facts (factQueryDeprecated0130/factFormDeprecated0130) with factQueryRemoved0130/factFormRemoved0130 in the exact same narrow-regex style (no parser growth), updated their registrations and docsguard_test.go fixtures accordingly, and confirmed the real docs/cmd/docsguard binary reports zero violations. Verified via git diff --stat that VERSION, package.json, go.mod's go/toolchain directives, go.sum, yarn.lock, release workflow files, and static/js/dist + static/css/dist are byte-identical to base (not touched at all) -- the frontend rebuild-and-diff gate in verify.sh independently confirms zero frontend asset diff. Full ./scripts/verify.sh green (gofmt, golangci-lint, go mod verify, go vet, go build, go test, ansible bootstrap check, docs canonical examples/docsguard, go test -race, frontend rebuild diff, action pins, govulncheck), plus gosec (12 pre-existing baseline findings, all outside this PR's diff -- none new), gitleaks (no leaks), actionlint (clean), and zizmor (no findings) all green. Ran the full Playwright/browser suite via scripts/test-browser.sh (TestBrowser* under -tags=browser): all green with zero frontend asset diff, confirming the SPA's browser flows are completely unaffected since it never sent an API key via any transport.

Independently verified every binding section of goal.md against the Builder's single commit by direct code and test-assertion reading, not Builder claims. Read middleware/middleware.go's extractExplicitAPICredential/RequireAPIKey end to end: confirmed query/form presence detection is independent of value (bare ?api_key with no = sets unsupportedTransport), unsupportedTransport is never folded into the values/ambiguity computation (values is built exclusively from Authorization headers), an identical-value coincidence with a valid Authorization header still rejects (unsupportedTransport is ORed unconditionally into RequireAPIKey's single rejection branch, ahead of/independent from the value/ambiguity checks), and present becomes true whenever unsupportedTransport is true even with zero Authorization headers (verified against the early-return guard's exact boolean expression). Read TestAPIAuthRateLimitUnsupportedTransportCountsAsOneFailure directly: the budget-depletion harness (burst=20) proves combined query+form and query/form+Authorization requests each consume exactly one failure unit per request, reusing RequireAPIKey's single existing limiter.ResolveClientIP/currentAPIAuthRateLimiter call sites (no second IP-resolution path). Confirmed via git diff main..HEAD -- '*csrf*' (empty) and a repo-wide grep for func Test.*CSRF that controllers/route_test.go (the only other CSRF-test file) has a zero-line diff -- the full existing CSRF suite is genuinely unmodified and still green; one new additive test (TestCSRFExceptionsRemovedTransportStillExempt) covers the new behavior. Confirmed via git diff --stat that no RBAC/permission file is touched. Read the full diff of all four canonical docs and internal/docsguard/docsguard.go end to end: query/form now read 'removed' (not 'deprecated, target 0.13.0') in all four; raw Authorization's deprecated-no-removal-version status and Bearer's canonical status are verbatim-unchanged in every doc; factQueryRemoved0130/factFormRemoved0130 replace the old facts with the identical three-regex narrow-literal style (no Markdown/HTML parsing growth); checkCanonicalExamples' actual exemption mechanics are unchanged, only its doc comment was extended. Independently re-verified via git diff main..HEAD (not just --stat) that VERSION, package.json, go.mod, go.sum, yarn.lock, .github/workflows/release.yml, and static/js/dist + static/css/dist are all byte-identical to base. Independently re-ran go build ./..., go vet ./..., full go test ./... (all packages ok), go test -race ./middleware/... (clean), and every test function named in goal.md sections 1/4/5/8/9 via WSL (TestExplicitAPICredentialExtraction 17 subtests, TestAPIAuthenticationMechanismSelection, TestCredentialAwareAPIProtection, TestCSRFExceptionsRemovedTransportStillExempt, TestAPIAuthRateLimitUnsupportedTransportCountsAsOneFailure 3 subtests, TestAPIAuthRateLimitBlockedIPRejectsRemovedTransportBeforeInspection 2 subtests, TestCampaignCompleteTransportDeprecationEquivalence 5 subtests, TestFormTransportPreservesBusinessFields 2 subtests, all docsguard TestCheckFile*/TestCheckAll* tests) -- all PASS. Independently re-verified the Builder's commit signature via git log -1 --format=fuller --show-signature run through WSL (native Windows git on this host has no gpg on PATH, confirmed directly via its own 'cannot spawn gpg' error rather than assumed -- an environment quirk, not a signing failure; WSL git, which actually performed the signing, shows the real result): Good signature from vg-kvr-grp <killian.vanruymbeke@vesperisgroup.com> (RSA key EB3E931B95880FB8931299E59DFC16E2E234C67B, ultimate trust), correct author/committer, zero Copilot mentions. No issues found.
